candidate_policy.observed_text:
For a general post-cleaning assessment of a demonstration bearing, inspection should cover: (1) raceways (inner and outer) for spalling, flaking, indentations, scoring, and wear patterns; (2) rolling elements for surface damage, cracking, and discoloration; (3) cage/retainer for deformation, cracks, wear, and looseness; (4) sealing/shielding and lubricant condition, including contamination and lubricant identity/specification/batch; (5) fits and seating surfaces (shaft and housing) for fretting, corrosion, and evidence of misalignment; (6) dimensional/clearance checks where applicable; and (7) general condition such as corrosion, discoloration/heat effects, and cleanliness. Context factors relevant to any reuse consideration include: the bearing's service history and loading/speed environment; the assumed mounting misalignment (a teaching assumption here, not an observed cause); lubricant type, condition, and contamination; the intended application and its criticality; applicable model-specific acceptance criteria and thresholds; and any required authorization (e.g., aviation or reuse approval), which is not supplied here. Smooth hand rotation alone would not approve reuse: free rotation only indicates the bearing is not seized or grossly obstructed and does not establish raceway/rolling-element integrity, correct clearance, lubricant suitability, or fitness for the intended application. Reuse decisions require the full inspection results plus the missing case-specific records and authorized acceptance criteria.
Scope is registered generic bearing education only; no model-specific thresholds, device records, lubricant identity/specification/batch, sampling quantity, or aviation/reuse authorization were supplied.
The shaft-housing misalignment is an independently specified teaching assumption, not an observed cause or classifier inference; no actual damage cause is inferred.
The predicted class 'inner_race' is a caller-assigned module input, not a result of a real classifier or task model.
